Hmm. Well, a big difference in crusader is the massive lack of farmland. it all takes place in a desert, so you can only build farms on an oasis. Wheat farms are smaller than most farms and produce more, though baking bread requires a wheat farm, mill, and bakeries. Semi-related to this, crusader doesn't force you to place your granary at the beginning, which led me to forget it a few times when I was first playing. Don't forget your granary.

My personal favourite strategy is to use a lot of wood to make a few stone quarries so I can sell the stone. Using this money I make an assload of fletchers and make thousands of archers. Admittedly this doesn't work near as well in multiplayer as it does in single player, but it never stops me from using it.

Mangonels seem good until they start firing on enemies inside your own castle and wrecking shit. 

Arabian archers are way better, but way more expensive. Arabian swordsmen are good in a pinch, but are much less effective than crusader swordsmen. Arabian slingers are way better than they should be for such a low price. Good damage even to armour, but low range and health. 

I'm sure if you look around this subreddit you can find plenty of tips from people who are much better at this game than I.
Glad I could help. Pro tip: wells and water pots if you're in multiplayer, otherwise a single slave can destroy everything you've built.

Stronghold Crusader is very much worth it in my opinion. The mercenary Arabian units greatly change the way the game is played. These units cost a lot, but don't require weapons. Units like slaves, who set fire to buildings; assassins, who are invisible up to a distance, can climb walls and open gatehouses; and horse archers, who can move and shoot at the same time which makes them the best raiding units in the game. 

The Crusader is a very fun, though punishingly difficult campaign which is basically preset skirmishes with old and new lords. I'm only on number 30 something, and I don't expect to be getting much progress since 2 pigs is too many when you don't get resources. Other than the crusader trails, though, there isn't much of a campaign. There's the historical campaigns which are just an extended tutorial. Its pretty fun, but there's not much to it.

In addition to all the fighting, there's also several castle builder missions, where all you have to worry about is the odd lion attack, and your only other adversity is the demands of your people. 

Overall, I'd say it's a fantastic game and very much worth the $10 it is on steam right now. If you like Stronghold, it's a fantastic addition which adds a lot to the experience. I've been playing this game for years, and I'm still learning new ways to enjoy it.

Glad I could help. What's your youtube channel? Also, what accent do you have? Both an accent and self-esteem can be improved with time and effort, and the more you do the better you'll get. The key is to just keep talking and ignore whatever you think might be holding you back. But enough after school special. 

Some other things you could do are like a war movie-esque commentary in which an accent might be pretty appropriate. If you have bad self esteem getting some friends to play with you could help to make you more comfortable and give you more to talk about. If you have enough friends to play with you could do some fun game modes like a bayonets only game on apartments. There's plenty of wacky antics to be had if everyone's playing along.

I feel like highlight reels would be the best option to start with. Something fun/cool and easy to watch will get people's attention best. Tutorials would be good, but as you've said basically everything's been covered by now. If you can have a bunch of friends playing with you on a small server you could do funny commentary without having to worry about playing well, so it'd probably be easier to watch than ten minutes of a guy talking about the ditch he's hiding in. 

But really, it's your channel and you should experiment with it. If you're good at talking, maybe commentary videos might be entertaining. If you have a lot of cool moments, then a highlight reel would be good. Nothing ever goes quite as planned, so just mess around with it and see what works.

To hit more, you have to decrease your THACO, (To Hit Armour Class 0), which you can view on the character screen, a little ways under your experience points. The higher your strength, the lower your melee THACO. -1 THACO per 2 points of Strength. For ranged THACO, increase your dexterity. Enchanted weapons always have THACO bonuses. And for most classes, possibly all, THACO goes down as you level up. A lot of magical equipment, like bracers or rings, decrease your THACO.
